    <section id="wpx-what-template--23313745805555__gym_cleaning_procurement_XxKVAn" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>What is gym cleaning procurement?</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">Gym cleaning procurement is the process a fitness facility uses to source, standardize, purchase, and reorder its cleaning supplies as a recurring operational category — not a one-time retail purchase. For wipes specifically, it covers supplier selection, format decisions, bulk ordering, dispenser deployment, inventory, and replenishment cadence.</p><div class="wpx-liferow">
          <div class="wpx-liferow__body">
            <p>The distinction matters because a commercial gym doesn't buy cleaning wipes the way a household does. Wipes are a consumable that a facility burns through every operating day, at every cleaning point, for as long as the doors are open. Treated as a retail item, that becomes a stream of small, reactive purchases. Treated as procurement, it becomes a planned supply program with a chosen supplier, a standardized product, and a predictable reorder rhythm.</p>
            <p>Everything downstream — cost per wipe, staff time spent restocking, whether stations ever run dry, how easily you can open a second location — flows from how deliberately you set that program up. For the fitness-specific product range referenced throughout, see the <a href="https://wipex.co/collections/fitness">Wipex commercial fitness collection</a>.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="wpx-liferow__media">

    <section id="wpx-framework-template--23313745805555__gym_cleaning_procurement_XxKVAn" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>The gym cleaning procurement framework</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">A sound procurement program moves in a repeatable sequence: define the need, specify the product, select a supplier, choose the format, place a bulk order, and establish replenishment. Done once well, it repeats at every station and every location.</p>
      <div class="wpx-flow" role="img" aria-label="Procurement flow: need, specification, supplier, format, bulk order, replenishment, standardization">
        <span class="wpx-flow__step">Need</span><span class="wpx-flow__arw" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
        <span class="wpx-flow__step">Specification</span><span class="wpx-flow__arw" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
        <span class="wpx-flow__step">Supplier</span><span class="wpx-flow__arw" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
        <span class="wpx-flow__step">Format</span><span class="wpx-flow__arw" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
        <span class="wpx-flow__step">Bulk Order</span><span class="wpx-flow__arw" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
        <span class="wpx-flow__step">Replenishment</span><span class="wpx-flow__arw" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
        <span class="wpx-flow__step wpx-flow__step--end">Standardization</span>
      </div>
      <p><strong>What procurement teams should evaluate.</strong> At the specification stage, confirm the product actually fits the surfaces in your facility: equipment upholstery, vinyl, rubber grips, cardio consoles, and studio mats. At the supplier stage, confirm one vendor can support the whole chain — the wipe, a bulk format, a compatible dispenser, and consistent restock — so you're not stitching a system together from multiple sources.</p>
      <p><strong>Recommended approach.</strong> Standardize on the fewest SKUs that still cover every station type. Fewer SKUs means simpler ordering, easier staff training, and cleaner inventory — the operational payoff of treating this as procurement rather than ad-hoc buying.</p><figure class="wpx-lifeband wpx-life wpx-life--16x9 wpx-life--overlay" style="--wpx-img-pos:center;">
          <img src="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/Ultra-realistic_commercial_photography_premium_pr-1788185703905.webp?v=1788185834&width=1120"

    <section id="wpx-format-template--23313745805555__gym_cleaning_procurement_XxKVAn" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>How to choose the right wipe format</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">Match format to how each station is used and how much volume it sees. Canisters and buckets suit lower-volume or portable points; bulk refill rolls suit high-volume floors; dispensers paired with refills suit fixed, member-facing stations.</p>
      <h3>Canisters and buckets</h3>
      <p>Self-contained formats are the flexible unit of a supply program. A <a href="https://wipex.co/products/natural-gym-wipes-buckets">400ct dispensing bucket</a> is easy to place at a front desk, a secondary studio, or a functional-training zone, and it doubles as portable backup during peak hours. These carry a higher cost per wipe than bulk, so they're best used to complement a bulk core rather than power a busy floor on their own.</p>
      <h3>Bulk refill rolls</h3>
      <p>For high-volume use, a bulk refill roll is the most efficient procurement unit. Instead of handling many small containers, staff feed a large roll into a dispenser and reload far less often. The <a href="https://wipex.co/products/natural-gym-wipes-bulk-refill-roll">Wipex 700ct bulk gym refill roll</a> uses large 8"×8" wipes and fits most wall- and floor-mounted dispensers, which keeps cost per wipe low and reorder cadence predictable.</p>
      <h3>Dispensers as the station layer</h3>
      <p>Dispensers turn a bulk roll into a standardized cleaning station. Wall-mounted units preserve floor space in corridors and cardio rows; a <a href="https://wipex.co/products/floor-dispenser">free-standing floor dispenser</a> creates a visible, member-facing point in open zones and studios. Standardizing on one or two dispenser types across the facility keeps refills interchangeable and restocking uniform.</p>
      <p class="wpx-inline-cta"><a data-cro="proc-format-disp" href="https://wipex.co/collections/dispensers">Explore gym wipe dispensers →</a></p>
    </section><div class="wpx-videoband">
        <div class="wpx-vid"><video playsinline="true" autoplay="autoplay" loop="loop" muted="muted" preload="metadata" class="wpx-vid__media" poster="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/preview_images/5ecbc6829a0c4246ba6cb0da1e36d2be.thumbnail.0000000000_1600x.jpg?v=1787081408"><source src="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/videos/c/vp/5ecbc6829a0c4246ba6cb0da1e36d2be/5ecbc6829a0c4246ba6cb0da1e36d2be.HD-1080p-7.2Mbps-91970295.mp4?v=0" type="video/mp4"><img src="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/preview_images/5ecbc6829a0c4246ba6cb0da1e36d2be.thumbnail.0000000000_1600x.jpg?v=1787081408"></video></div>
      </div><section id="wpx-bulk-template--23313745805555__gym_cleaning_procurement_XxKVAn" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>Bulk vs. individual purchasing</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">No single model is universally best. The right mix depends on station volume, how much handling your team can absorb, and how many points you're supplying.</p>
      <div class="wpx-tablewrap" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Procurement model comparison">
        <table class="wpx-table">
          <thead><tr><th scope="col">Procurement model</th><th scope="col">Operational effect</th><th scope="col">Best for</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr><td>Small individual containers</td><td>More frequent replenishment, higher cost per wipe</td><td>Lower-volume / secondary stations</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Dispensing bucket (400ct)</td><td>Flexible, portable supply</td><td>Front desk, studios, backup stock</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Bulk refill roll (700ct)</td><td>Fewer refill events, lower cost per wipe</td><td>High-volume commercial floors</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Dispenser + refill</td><td>Standardized, member-facing station</td><td>Fixed commercial cleaning points</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Standardized SKU program</td><td>Consistent ordering across sites</td><td>Multi-location & franchise operators</td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="wpx-cost-template--23313745805555__gym_cleaning_procurement_XxKVAn" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>Cost and value: what to calculate</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">Instead of chasing a headline discount, evaluate total cost of ownership: cost per wipe, replenishment labor, storage, and station availability. The cheapest unit price isn't always the lowest real cost.</p>
      <p>Two simple calculations let you compare options on your own numbers rather than borrowed ones:</p>
      <p class="wpx-formula"><strong>Cost per wipe = total product cost ÷ usable wipes</strong><br><strong>Monthly wipe demand ≈ average daily usage × operating days</strong></p>
      <p>These are illustrative formulas, not fixed figures — plug in your observed usage. The value of bulk formats usually shows up in two places the sticker price hides: a lower cost per wipe at volume, and less staff time spent handling and swapping containers. A busy station that a team reloads once from a 700ct roll costs far less in labor than one refilled repeatedly from small containers. Factor storage too: bulk formats consume less shelf space per wipe than an equivalent count of individual canisters.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="wpx-500-template--23313745805555__gym_cleaning_procurement_XxKVAn" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>How a 500-member gym could approach procurement</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">A mid-size commercial gym should build its program around bulk refill fed into fixed dispensers, with buckets and canisters as flexible backup — then set a reorder trigger so supply is never reactive.</p><div class="wpx-liferow wpx-liferow--rev">
          <div class="wpx-liferow__media">
            <figure class="wpx-life wpx-life--2x3" style="--wpx-img-pos:center;">
              <img src="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/edit.png?v=1787849847&width=480"
                srcset="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/edit.png?v=1787849847&width=360 360w, //wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/edit.png?v=1787849847&width=480 480w, //wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/edit.png?v=1787849847&width=720 720w"
                sizes="(max-width:900px) 90vw, 26vw" width="480" height="720"
                alt="Operations manager counting cleaning stations and planning reorder cadence"
                loading="lazy" decoding="async">
            </figure></div>
          <div class="wpx-liferow__body">
            <p>The point of an example isn't a fixed shopping list; every facility differs. It's a workflow you can run on your own floor — count your stations, estimate demand from your own usage, choose a bulk core, and lock in a reorder cadence before supply becomes reactive.</p>
          </div>
        </div><p>Run the following workflow on your own floor:</p>
      <ol class="wpx-steps">
        <li><strong>Identify every cleaning station.</strong> Walk the floor and count natural points: cardio rows, strength stations, free weights, functional zones, and studios.</li>
        <li><strong>Estimate daily wipe demand.</strong> Use your own observed usage per station, not borrowed averages.</li>
        <li><strong>Select a primary format.</strong> For most mid-size gyms, that's a bulk refill roll as the core.</li>
        <li><strong>Decide dispenser needs.</strong> One dispenser per fixed, member-facing station; standardize the type.</li>
        <li><strong>Set backup inventory.</strong> Keep buckets and canisters for peak days and new stations.</li>
        <li><strong>Define a reorder trigger.</strong> Reorder when on-hand stock hits a set number of rolls, not when you run out.</li>
        <li><strong>Standardize and schedule.</strong> Lock the SKUs and set a recurring purchasing cadence.</li>
      </ol>
      <p class="wpx-inline-cta"><a data-cro="proc-500-quote" href="https://wipex.co/collections/wipe-dispensers">Talk to Wipex about a bulk supply plan →</a></p>
    </section>

    <section id="wpx-multi-template--23313745805555__gym_cleaning_procurement_XxKVAn" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>Multi-location and franchise standardization</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">For operators running two, five, or a full franchise network, the biggest procurement win is standardization: the same wipe, format, dispenser, and reorder process at every site.</p>
      <p>When each location sources its own supplies, you get drift — different products, inconsistent stations, uneven member experience, and purchasing that's impossible to forecast. Standardizing a single system across sites simplifies almost everything downstream: staff training becomes one process instead of many, inventory is comparable location to location, reordering follows one cadence, and opening a new site is a rollout of a known setup rather than a fresh sourcing project each time.</p>

      <h2>Frequently asked questions</h2>
      <div class="wpx-faq" data-wpx-faq>
  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>What is gym cleaning procurement?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>Gym cleaning procurement is the process a fitness facility uses to source, standardize, purchase, and reorder cleaning supplies as an ongoing operating category rather than as occasional retail purchases. For wipes, it typically includes supplier selection, format decisions, dispenser setup, inventory planning, and reorder timing.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>How should a gym buy cleaning supplies in bulk?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>Most gyms buy cleaning supplies in bulk by standardizing one primary wipe format, estimating demand from actual station usage, and setting a recurring reorder cadence. High-volume facilities often use refill rolls as the core format because they reduce handling and support fixed dispensers, while buckets or canisters can serve as backup for smaller or portable stations.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>What should a gym look for in a cleaning supply supplier?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>A gym should look for a supplier that offers equipment-safe wipes, reliable refill availability, dispenser compatibility, and consistent reordering support. It also helps if the supplier can support the same system across different station types or multiple locations, which makes training, purchasing, and inventory control easier to standardize.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>Are bulk refill rolls better for commercial gyms?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>For many high-volume commercial gyms, bulk refill rolls are more efficient than small canisters because they hold more wipes, reduce refill frequency, and make it easier to standardize stations across the floor. Smaller containers can still work well in lower-volume or portable settings, so the right format depends on traffic, layout, and staffing.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>How often should a commercial gym reorder cleaning wipes?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>Commercial gyms should reorder cleaning wipes based on an inventory trigger rather than waiting to run out. A practical approach is to estimate monthly demand from average daily usage and operating days, then set a minimum on-hand stock level for each primary format. That makes reordering more predictable and reduces the chance of empty stations during busy periods.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>How should fitness franchises standardize cleaning supplies?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>Fitness franchises usually standardize cleaning supplies by selecting a small set of approved SKUs, such as one primary wipe, one refill format, and one or two dispenser types, then deploying them the same way across locations. This simplifies staff training, inventory management, reordering, and new-site setup.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>What cleaning supplies should a 500-member gym buy?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>A 500-member gym typically needs a cleaning setup built around member-facing wipe stations, backup stock, and a reorder plan based on real usage. Many facilities of that size use fixed dispensers with refill rolls at primary stations, then keep buckets or canisters available for studios, overflow demand, or secondary areas.</p>
    </div>
  </details>

  <details class="wpx-faq__item">
    <summary>Where can commercial gyms source cleaning wipes in bulk?</summary>
    <div class="wpx-faq__a">
      <p>Commercial gyms can source cleaning wipes in bulk from commercial janitorial suppliers, facility supply vendors, or fitness-focused cleaning suppliers that offer wipes, refill formats, and compatible dispensers together. When comparing vendors, look at product compatibility, refill availability, dispenser support, and how well the supplier can support recurring commercial orders.</p>
    </div>
  </details>
</div>

  <script>
function getVariantFromURL() {
    const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    const variant = urlParams.get('variant');
    console.log("Extracted Variant ID:", variant);
    return variant;
}

function getProductIdFromLoopWidget() {
    if (typeof LOOP_WIDGET === 'undefined') {
        console.log("LOOP_WIDGET is not defined.");
        return null;
    }

    const productIds = Object.keys(LOOP_WIDGET);
    if (productIds.length === 0) {
        console.log("No product ID found in LOOP_WIDGET.");
        return null;
    }

    const pid = productIds[0];
    console.log("Extracted Product ID from LOOP_WIDGET:", pid);
    return pid;
}

function handleVariantChange() {
    const variantId = getVariantFromURL();
    if (!variantId) {
        console.log("No variant ID found in URL.");
        return;
    }

    const pid = getProductIdFromLoopWidget();
    if (!pid) {
        console.log("Failed to get product ID.");
        return;
    }

    const inputElement = document.querySelector('input[name="product-id"]');
    if (inputElement && window?.LoopSubscriptions) {
        setTimeout(() => {
            console.log(
                "Updating LoopSubscriptions with product ID:",
                inputElement.value,
                "and variant ID:",
                variantId
            );
            window.LoopSubscriptions.handleLoopWidgetVariantIdChange(
                Number(inputElement.value),
                Number(variantId)
            );
        }, 0);
    } else {
        console.warn("LoopSubscriptions or product-id input not available.");
    }
}

// Run on page load
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", handleVariantChange);

// Listen for SPA URL changes (history API manipulation)
(function () {
    let lastUrl = location.href;

    new MutationObserver(() => {
        if (location.href !== lastUrl) {
            lastUrl = location.href;
            console.log("URL changed, re-running variant check.");
            handleVariantChange();
        }
    }).observe(document, { subtree: true, childList: true });

    window.addEventListener('popstate', handleVariantChange);
})();
</script>

<script>
      // Function to fetch the cart information via AJAX
    function updateCart() {
        $.ajax({
            url: '/cart.js',
            dataType: 'json',
            success: function(cartData) {
               var cartTotal = cartData.total_price;
                var itemCount = cartData.item_count;
               $('.cart-link__bubble').text(itemCount);
              const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
              const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
              
              if(cartTotal > 0){
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'block';
                
                updateProgressBar(cartTotal,itemCount);
              }else{
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'none';
               
              }
               
            },
            error: function(jqXHR, textStatus, errorThrown) {
                console.error('Error updating cart:', errorThrown);
            }
        });
    }

    updateCart();
    setInterval(updateCart, 500);
  
    function updateProgressBar(cartTotal, itemCount) {
      const progressWrapper = document.getElementById('cart-progress-wrapper');
    
      const progressThreshold = parseInt(progressWrapper.dataset.threshold, 10);
      const preGoalMessageTemplate = progressWrapper.dataset.preGoalMessageTemplate;
      const postGoalMessage = progressWrapper.dataset.postGoalMessage;
    
      const progressBar = document.getElementById('cart-progress-bar');
      const percntcstmId = document.getElementById('percntcstmId');
      
      const goalMessageElement = document.querySelector('.goal-message');
      
      const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
      const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
      
      
      if (itemCount === 0 || cartTotal === 0) {
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'none';
        }
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
        }
       
      } else {
       
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'block'; 
        }
        if (progressBar) {
          progressBar.style.display = 'block';
          const progressPercentage = Math.min((cartTotal / progressThreshold) * 100, 100); 
          progressBar.style.width = `${progressPercentage}%`;
            percntcstmId.textContent =`${progressPercentage.toFixed(2)}%`;
    
          if (progressPercentage >= 100) {
            progressWrapper.classList.add('full');
          } else {
            progressWrapper.classList.remove('full');
          }
        }
      
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
          let remainingForGoal = progressThreshold - cartTotal;
      
          if (remainingForGoal < 0) {
            remainingForGoal = 0;
          }
      
          const remainingAmountFormatted = `$${(remainingForGoal / 100).toFixed(2)}`;
          const preGoalMessage = preGoalMessageTemplate.replace('[remainingForGoalFormatted]', remainingAmountFormatted);
          goalMessageElement.innerHTML = remainingForGoal > 0
            ? preGoalMessage
            : postGoalMessage;
        }
      }
    }

        <h3>Clear</h3><p>Remove dishes, glassware, and debris the moment the party leaves.</p>

          <div class="wpx-flow__cell"><span class="k">Best practice</span><p>Clear in one confident pass; never leave a table half-done.</p></div>

          <div class="wpx-flow__cell"><span class="k">Operational impact</span><p>Every trip pulls the busser off the floor and delays the reset.</p></div>
          <div class="wpx-flow__cell"><span class="k">Best practice</span><p>Keep pre-moistened wipes within arm's reach at each station.</p></div>

        <div class="wpx-flow__grid">
          <div class="wpx-flow__cell"><span class="k">Common bottleneck</span><p>Every busser resets differently, so quality is inconsistent.</p></div>
          <div class="wpx-flow__cell"><span class="k">Operational impact</span><p>Inconsistent tables force servers to fix them before seating.</p></div>

      <div class="wpx-flow__panel" id="fp3-template--23346160206067__table_bussers_blog_p9TMzq" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="ftab3-template--23346160206067__table_bussers_blog_p9TMzq" tabindex="0" hidden>

          <div class="wpx-flow__cell"><span class="k">Operational impact</span><p>Empty-but-ready tables sit unseated during your busiest window.</p></div>
          <div class="wpx-flow__cell"><span class="k">Best practice</span><p>Use a simple, visible cue the whole team recognizes.</p></div>

        </div>

The role keeps the dining room flowing and directly affects how quickly tables can be turned.</div></details>
      <details><summary>How does a busser help with table turnover?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a">By clearing on sight, cleaning immediately, and resetting to a consistent standard, a busser shortens the gap between one party leaving and the next being seated — which increases seatings during peak hours.</div></details>
      <details><summary>What should a busser clean between guests?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a">The tabletop and high-touch surfaces the party used, including table edges, condiment caddies, and menus where applicable, plus a quick check of seating.   <script>
function getVariantFromURL() {
    const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    const variant = urlParams.get('variant');
    console.log("Extracted Variant ID:", variant);
    return variant;
}

function getProductIdFromLoopWidget() {
    if (typeof LOOP_WIDGET === 'undefined') {
        console.log("LOOP_WIDGET is not defined.");
        return null;
    }

    const productIds = Object.keys(LOOP_WIDGET);
    if (productIds.length === 0) {
        console.log("No product ID found in LOOP_WIDGET.");
        return null;
    }

    const pid = productIds[0];
    console.log("Extracted Product ID from LOOP_WIDGET:", pid);
    return pid;
}

function handleVariantChange() {
    const variantId = getVariantFromURL();
    if (!variantId) {
        console.log("No variant ID found in URL.");
        return;
    }

    const pid = getProductIdFromLoopWidget();
    if (!pid) {
        console.log("Failed to get product ID.");
        return;
    }

    const inputElement = document.querySelector('input[name="product-id"]');
    if (inputElement && window?.LoopSubscriptions) {
        setTimeout(() => {
            console.log(
                "Updating LoopSubscriptions with product ID:",
                inputElement.value,
                "and variant ID:",
                variantId
            );
            window.LoopSubscriptions.handleLoopWidgetVariantIdChange(
                Number(inputElement.value),
                Number(variantId)
            );
        }, 0);
    } else {
        console.warn("LoopSubscriptions or product-id input not available.");
    }
}

// Run on page load
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", handleVariantChange);

// Listen for SPA URL changes (history API manipulation)
(function () {
    let lastUrl = location.href;

    new MutationObserver(() => {
        if (location.href !== lastUrl) {
            lastUrl = location.href;
            console.log("URL changed, re-running variant check.");
            handleVariantChange();
        }
    }).observe(document, { subtree: true, childList: true });

    window.addEventListener('popstate', handleVariantChange);
})();
</script>

      // Function to fetch the cart information via AJAX
    function updateCart() {
        $.ajax({
            url: '/cart.js',
            dataType: 'json',
            success: function(cartData) {
               var cartTotal = cartData.total_price;
                var itemCount = cartData.item_count;
               $('.cart-link__bubble').text(itemCount);
              const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
              const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
              
              if(cartTotal > 0){
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'block';
                
                updateProgressBar(cartTotal,itemCount);
              }else{
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'none';
               
              }
               
            },
            error: function(jqXHR, textStatus, errorThrown) {
                console.error('Error updating cart:', errorThrown);
            }
        });
    }

    updateCart();
    setInterval(updateCart, 500);
  
    function updateProgressBar(cartTotal, itemCount) {
      const progressWrapper = document.getElementById('cart-progress-wrapper');
    
      const progressThreshold = parseInt(progressWrapper.dataset.threshold, 10);
      const preGoalMessageTemplate = progressWrapper.dataset.preGoalMessageTemplate;
      const postGoalMessage = progressWrapper.dataset.postGoalMessage;
    
      const progressBar = document.getElementById('cart-progress-bar');
      const percntcstmId = document.getElementById('percntcstmId');
      
      const goalMessageElement = document.querySelector('.goal-message');
      
      const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
      const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
      
      
      if (itemCount === 0 || cartTotal === 0) {
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'none';
        }
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
        }
       
      } else {
       
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'block'; 
        }
        if (progressBar) {
          progressBar.style.display = 'block';
          const progressPercentage = Math.min((cartTotal / progressThreshold) * 100, 100); 
          progressBar.style.width = `${progressPercentage}%`;
            percntcstmId.textContent =`${progressPercentage.toFixed(2)}%`;
    
          if (progressPercentage >= 100) {
            progressWrapper.classList.add('full');
          } else {
            progressWrapper.classList.remove('full');
          }
        }
      
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
          let remainingForGoal = progressThreshold - cartTotal;
      
          if (remainingForGoal < 0) {
            remainingForGoal = 0;
          }
      
          const remainingAmountFormatted = `$${(remainingForGoal / 100).toFixed(2)}`;
          const preGoalMessage = preGoalMessageTemplate.replace('[remainingForGoalFormatted]', remainingAmountFormatted);
          goalMessageElement.innerHTML = remainingForGoal > 0
            ? preGoalMessage
            : postGoalMessage;
        }
      }
    }

      <h2>What cleaning supplies does a commercial gym need?</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">A commercial gym needs equipment-safe wipes, a bulk supply format, dispensers to hold them, and a repeatable way to keep every station stocked. Together those pieces form a cleaning system rather than a shelf of loose products.</p>
      <p>Most facilities start by buying canisters of wipes and stop there. That works for a small studio, but it breaks down quickly in a high-traffic environment: stations run dry at peak hours, staff spend time chasing empty containers, and members are left without a way to wipe down equipment. The fix isn't more canisters — it's a supply model built around bulk volume and fixed, refillable stations.</p><div class="wpx-liferow">
          <div class="wpx-liferow__body">
            <p>For fitness environments specifically, the wipes themselves matter. Equipment upholstery, vinyl, rubber grips, cardio consoles, and studio mats all sit in the same room, so a general-purpose janitorial wipe isn't always the right tool. Wipex fitness equipment wipes are designed for these surfaces — made to clean sweat and grime on machines, benches, and accessories without the harshness of industrial cleaners.</p>
            <p class="wpx-inline-cta"><a data-cro="gym-need-link" href="https://wipex.co/collections/fitness">Explore Wipex commercial fitness wipes →</a></p>

    <section id="wpx-system-template--23313656938739__wipex_gym_cleaning_system_pcCCEb" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>What is a professional gym cleaning system?</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">A professional gym cleaning system is the combination of equipment-safe wipes, a bulk or refill format, dispensers, placed cleaning stations, and a replenishment routine — designed so cleaning happens consistently without staff intervention at every step.</p>
      <p><strong>Why this matters.</strong> Individual products solve a moment. A system solves a facility. When wipes, format, and dispensers are chosen together, you get predictable cost per wipe, stations that stay stocked, and a member experience that looks and feels professional throughout the day.</p>
      <p><strong>How to think about it.</strong> Picture the flow of a single wipe from storeroom to station: what format arrives on your dock, how it loads into a dispenser, where that dispenser lives on the floor, and how quickly a staff member can reload it. When each of those steps is intentional, replenishment becomes a two-minute task instead of a recurring problem.</p>

    <section id="wpx-formats-template--23313656938739__wipex_gym_cleaning_system_pcCCEb" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>Wipes, bulk refill rolls, and dispensers: what to buy</h2>
      <p class="wpx-lead">Choose the format by how the station is used. Canisters suit small or portable points, bulk refill rolls suit busy floors, and dispensers with refills suit fixed, member-facing stations.</p>

      <h3>Commercial gym wipes (canisters)</h3>
      <p>Canister wipes are the flexible unit of the system. They're easy to place at a front desk, in an office, at a secondary studio, or as backup stock. For a small facility with light traffic, canisters alone may be enough. As volume grows, they become the supplement to a bulk-and-dispenser setup rather than the core of it.</p>

      <h3>Bulk gym wipe refill rolls</h3>
      <p>A bulk refill roll is the most cost-effective format for high-volume use. Instead of buying and discarding many small containers, you feed a large roll into a dispenser and reload far less often. The Wipex 700ct gym refill roll is built for exactly this — large 8"×8" wipes designed to fit most wall- and floor-mounted dispensers, which keeps the cost per wipe low and the reorder cadence predictable.</p>
      <p class="wpx-inline-cta"><a data-cro="gym-formats-refill" href="https://wipex.co/products/natural-gym-wipes-bulk-refill-roll">Shop the 700ct bulk gym refill roll →</a></p>

      <h3>Gym wipe dispensers and cleaning stations</h3>
      <p>Dispensers turn a roll into a station. A wall-mounted unit preserves floor space in tight corridors and cardio rows; a free-standing floor dispenser creates a visible, member-facing cleaning point in open zones and studios; and an XL bucket dispenser works as a high-capacity or portable option for garages, functional-training areas, and overflow. Placing dispensers where members already pause — end of a machine row, studio entrance, free-weight area — is what makes wiping down a habit rather than an ask.</p>

      <p class="wpx-lead">A mid-size commercial gym with strong daily traffic should plan around fixed dispenser stations fed by bulk refill rolls, with canisters as backup — not around loose containers alone.</p><div class="wpx-liferow wpx-liferow--rev">

            </figure></div>
          <div class="wpx-liferow__body">
            <p>The point of an example like this isn't a fixed shopping list; every facility's usage differs. It's a way to reason about the decision. Walk your floor and count the natural cleaning points: cardio rows, strength stations, free-weight areas, functional zones, and any studios. Each of those is a candidate for a dispenser. The more of them you can serve from a single bulk format, the simpler your ordering becomes.</p>
            <p>A practical way to estimate your own volume without guessing is a simple formula:</p>
          </div>

Keep a small buffer of canisters for peak days and new stations so a busy afternoon never leaves a station empty.</p>

      <p>Wipex is a wipes and dispensing brand built around commercial fitness use: bulk gym wipes, 700ct refill rolls, and wall, floor, and bucket dispensers that work together as cleaning stations across gyms, Pilates studios, yoga studios, and wellness facilities. That specialization is what makes it straightforward to roll out one standardized system — and repeat it at every location.</p>
    </section><section id="wpx-faq-template--23313656938739__wipex_gym_cleaning_system_pcCCEb" class="wpx-block">
      <h2>Frequently asked questions</h2>
      <div class="wpx-faq" data-wpx-faq>
        <details class="wpx-faq__item"><summary>What is an effective cleaning system for a commercial gym?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a"><p>An effective cleaning system for a commercial gym usually includes equipment-safe wipes, fixed dispensers placed throughout the facility, and a refill process staff can follow consistently. The goal is to keep wipes easy for members to reach while making restocking predictable for staff. High-traffic gyms often prefer refill-based systems because they reduce stockouts and simplify supply management across multiple cleaning stations.</p></div></details>
        <details class="wpx-faq__item"><summary>What cleaning supplies does a commercial gym need?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a"><p>At minimum, a commercial gym needs equipment-safe wipes, dispensers or wipe stations, refill stock, and a process for monitoring and replacing used supplies. Many facilities also separate member-facing cleaning supplies from staff cleaning supplies used for floors, locker rooms, and restrooms. For equipment areas, the priority is a wipe system that is easy to access, safe on surfaces, and simple to replenish.</p></div></details>
        <details class="wpx-faq__item"><summary>What should gyms look for in bulk gym wipes?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a"><p>When choosing bulk gym wipes, commercial gyms should look for wipes that are safe for fitness equipment, compatible with their dispensers, and practical for high-volume use. Useful comparison points include wipe size, refill count, case quantity, dispenser fit, and how often stations need restocking. For high-traffic facilities, bulk refill formats are often preferred because they support more consistent stocking across multiple workout zones.</p></div></details>
        <details class="wpx-faq__item"><summary>How do you choose the right gym wipe dispenser?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a"><p>The right gym wipe dispenser depends on layout, traffic, and how visible you want cleaning stations to be. Wall-mounted dispensers work well in narrow walkways and cardio rows where floor space is limited. Free-standing dispensers are more visible in open workout areas, while larger bucket-style dispensers can suit high-capacity or portable cleaning points. The best choice is the one that fits your refill format and keeps wipes consistently available.</p></div></details>
        <details class="wpx-faq__item"><summary>Are bulk refill rolls better than canisters for high-traffic gyms?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a"><p>In many high-traffic gyms, bulk refill rolls are more efficient than small canisters because they hold more wipes, reduce stockouts, and cut the time staff spend restocking stations. They are especially useful when the facility has multiple cleaning points that need the same refill format. Canisters may still work well in smaller spaces or as backup supplies, but refill systems are often easier to standardize at scale.</p></div></details>
        <details class="wpx-faq__item"><summary>What should a fitness facility look for in a cleaning supply supplier?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a"><p>A fitness facility should look for a supplier that offers equipment-safe wipes, dependable refill availability, dispenser compatibility, and consistent fulfillment. It also helps if the supplier can support the same system across different facility sizes or locations. Beyond product fit, operators should consider reorder reliability, packaging consistency, and whether the supplier makes it easy to standardize cleaning stations throughout the gym.</p></div></details>
        <details class="wpx-faq__item"><summary>How should a commercial gym set up cleaning stations?</summary><div class="wpx-faq__a"><p>Commercial gyms should place cleaning stations where members naturally transition between activities, such as cardio row exits, selectorized machine areas, free-weight zones, studio entrances, and functional training spaces. The goal is to keep wipes within easy reach of high-touch equipment without creating clutter. Using the same refill format across stations also makes staff training, restocking, and inventory control more consistent.</p></div></details>

Rather than buying only by unit price, operators should consider refill capacity, dispenser compatibility, restocking time, and backup supply needs. Standardizing one wipe format across the facility often makes ordering easier and reduces the risk of empty stations during busy periods.</p></div></details>

  <script>
function getVariantFromURL() {
    const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    const variant = urlParams.get('variant');
    console.log("Extracted Variant ID:", variant);
    return variant;
}

function getProductIdFromLoopWidget() {
    if (typeof LOOP_WIDGET === 'undefined') {
        console.log("LOOP_WIDGET is not defined.");
        return null;
    }

    const productIds = Object.keys(LOOP_WIDGET);
    if (productIds.length === 0) {
        console.log("No product ID found in LOOP_WIDGET.");
        return null;
    }

    const pid = productIds[0];
    console.log("Extracted Product ID from LOOP_WIDGET:", pid);
    return pid;
}

function handleVariantChange() {
    const variantId = getVariantFromURL();
    if (!variantId) {
        console.log("No variant ID found in URL.");
        return;
    }

    const pid = getProductIdFromLoopWidget();
    if (!pid) {
        console.log("Failed to get product ID.");
        return;
    }

    const inputElement = document.querySelector('input[name="product-id"]');
    if (inputElement && window?.LoopSubscriptions) {
        setTimeout(() => {
            console.log(
                "Updating LoopSubscriptions with product ID:",
                inputElement.value,
                "and variant ID:",
                variantId
            );
            window.LoopSubscriptions.handleLoopWidgetVariantIdChange(
                Number(inputElement.value),
                Number(variantId)
            );
        }, 0);
    } else {
        console.warn("LoopSubscriptions or product-id input not available.");
    }
}

// Run on page load
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", handleVariantChange);

// Listen for SPA URL changes (history API manipulation)
(function () {
    let lastUrl = location.href;

    new MutationObserver(() => {
        if (location.href !== lastUrl) {
            lastUrl = location.href;
            console.log("URL changed, re-running variant check.");
            handleVariantChange();
        }
    }).observe(document, { subtree: true, childList: true });

    window.addEventListener('popstate', handleVariantChange);
})();
</script>

      // Function to fetch the cart information via AJAX
    function updateCart() {
        $.ajax({
            url: '/cart.js',
            dataType: 'json',
            success: function(cartData) {
               var cartTotal = cartData.total_price;
                var itemCount = cartData.item_count;
               $('.cart-link__bubble').text(itemCount);
              const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
              const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
              
              if(cartTotal > 0){
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'block';
                
                updateProgressBar(cartTotal,itemCount);
              }else{
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'none';
               
              }
               
            },
            error: function(jqXHR, textStatus, errorThrown) {
                console.error('Error updating cart:', errorThrown);
            }
        });
    }

    updateCart();
    setInterval(updateCart, 500);
  
    function updateProgressBar(cartTotal, itemCount) {
      const progressWrapper = document.getElementById('cart-progress-wrapper');
    
      const progressThreshold = parseInt(progressWrapper.dataset.threshold, 10);
      const preGoalMessageTemplate = progressWrapper.dataset.preGoalMessageTemplate;
      const postGoalMessage = progressWrapper.dataset.postGoalMessage;
    
      const progressBar = document.getElementById('cart-progress-bar');
      const percntcstmId = document.getElementById('percntcstmId');
      
      const goalMessageElement = document.querySelector('.goal-message');
      
      const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
      const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
      
      
      if (itemCount === 0 || cartTotal === 0) {
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'none';
        }
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
        }
       
      } else {
       
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'block'; 
        }
        if (progressBar) {
          progressBar.style.display = 'block';
          const progressPercentage = Math.min((cartTotal / progressThreshold) * 100, 100); 
          progressBar.style.width = `${progressPercentage}%`;
            percntcstmId.textContent =`${progressPercentage.toFixed(2)}%`;
    
          if (progressPercentage >= 100) {
            progressWrapper.classList.add('full');
          } else {
            progressWrapper.classList.remove('full');
          }
        }
      
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
          let remainingForGoal = progressThreshold - cartTotal;
      
          if (remainingForGoal < 0) {
            remainingForGoal = 0;
          }
      
          const remainingAmountFormatted = `$${(remainingForGoal / 100).toFixed(2)}`;
          const preGoalMessage = preGoalMessageTemplate.replace('[remainingForGoalFormatted]', remainingAmountFormatted);
          goalMessageElement.innerHTML = remainingForGoal > 0
            ? preGoalMessage
            : postGoalMessage;
        }
      }
    }

  <script>
function getVariantFromURL() {
    const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    const variant = urlParams.get('variant');
    console.log("Extracted Variant ID:", variant);
    return variant;
}

function getProductIdFromLoopWidget() {
    if (typeof LOOP_WIDGET === 'undefined') {
        console.log("LOOP_WIDGET is not defined.");
        return null;
    }

    const productIds = Object.keys(LOOP_WIDGET);
    if (productIds.length === 0) {
        console.log("No product ID found in LOOP_WIDGET.");
        return null;
    }

    const pid = productIds[0];
    console.log("Extracted Product ID from LOOP_WIDGET:", pid);
    return pid;
}

function handleVariantChange() {
    const variantId = getVariantFromURL();
    if (!variantId) {
        console.log("No variant ID found in URL.");
        return;
    }

    const pid = getProductIdFromLoopWidget();
    if (!pid) {
        console.log("Failed to get product ID.");
        return;
    }

    const inputElement = document.querySelector('input[name="product-id"]');
    if (inputElement && window?.LoopSubscriptions) {
        setTimeout(() => {
            console.log(
                "Updating LoopSubscriptions with product ID:",
                inputElement.value,
                "and variant ID:",
                variantId
            );
            window.LoopSubscriptions.handleLoopWidgetVariantIdChange(
                Number(inputElement.value),
                Number(variantId)
            );
        }, 0);
    } else {
        console.warn("LoopSubscriptions or product-id input not available.");
    }
}

// Run on page load
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", handleVariantChange);

// Listen for SPA URL changes (history API manipulation)
(function () {
    let lastUrl = location.href;

    new MutationObserver(() => {
        if (location.href !== lastUrl) {
            lastUrl = location.href;
            console.log("URL changed, re-running variant check.");
            handleVariantChange();
        }
    }).observe(document, { subtree: true, childList: true });

    window.addEventListener('popstate', handleVariantChange);
})();
</script>

      // Function to fetch the cart information via AJAX
    function updateCart() {
        $.ajax({
            url: '/cart.js',
            dataType: 'json',
            success: function(cartData) {
               var cartTotal = cartData.total_price;
                var itemCount = cartData.item_count;
               $('.cart-link__bubble').text(itemCount);
              const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
              const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
              
              if(cartTotal > 0){
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'block';
                
                updateProgressBar(cartTotal,itemCount);
              }else{
                shipMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
                shipMessageElement2.style.display = 'none';
               
              }
               
            },
            error: function(jqXHR, textStatus, errorThrown) {
                console.error('Error updating cart:', errorThrown);
            }
        });
    }

    updateCart();
    setInterval(updateCart, 500);
  
    function updateProgressBar(cartTotal, itemCount) {
      const progressWrapper = document.getElementById('cart-progress-wrapper');
    
      const progressThreshold = parseInt(progressWrapper.dataset.threshold, 10);
      const preGoalMessageTemplate = progressWrapper.dataset.preGoalMessageTemplate;
      const postGoalMessage = progressWrapper.dataset.postGoalMessage;
    
      const progressBar = document.getElementById('cart-progress-bar');
      const percntcstmId = document.getElementById('percntcstmId');
      
      const goalMessageElement = document.querySelector('.goal-message');
      
      const shipMessageElement = document.querySelector('.cstm-announcement-bar-cls');
      const shipMessageElement2 = document.querySelector('.announcement-bar-shipping');
      
      
      if (itemCount === 0 || cartTotal === 0) {
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'none';
        }
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'none';
        }
       
      } else {
       
        if (progressWrapper) {
          progressWrapper.style.display = 'block'; 
        }
        if (progressBar) {
          progressBar.style.display = 'block';
          const progressPercentage = Math.min((cartTotal / progressThreshold) * 100, 100); 
          progressBar.style.width = `${progressPercentage}%`;
            percntcstmId.textContent =`${progressPercentage.toFixed(2)}%`;
    
          if (progressPercentage >= 100) {
            progressWrapper.classList.add('full');
          } else {
            progressWrapper.classList.remove('full');
          }
        }
      
        if (goalMessageElement) {
          goalMessageElement.style.display = 'block';
          let remainingForGoal = progressThreshold - cartTotal;
      
          if (remainingForGoal < 0) {
            remainingForGoal = 0;
          }
      
          const remainingAmountFormatted = `$${(remainingForGoal / 100).toFixed(2)}`;
          const preGoalMessage = preGoalMessageTemplate.replace('[remainingForGoalFormatted]', remainingAmountFormatted);
          goalMessageElement.innerHTML = remainingForGoal > 0
            ? preGoalMessage
            : postGoalMessage;
        }
      }
    }

      <p class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-eyebrow">Yoga Studio Operations · 2026</p>
      <h1 id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-h1" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-h1">
        Yoga Studio Hygiene Standards: What Members Expect in 2026
      </h1>
      <p class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-hero__intro">
        Hygiene is no longer a back-of-house task. In 2026, your members judge your studio by what they can see and touch — clean mats, fresh props, and cleaning supplies within reach. This is a practical, B2B guide for studio owners and operators who want a repeatable cleaning standard.
      </p>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-cta-row">
        <a class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-btn wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-btn--primary"
           href="/collections/fitness"
           data-cro="yoga-hygiene-hero-cta">
          Outfit Your Studio
          <span aria-hidden="true">→</span>
        </a>
        <a class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-btn wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-btn--ghost"
           href="/collections/yoga-mat-wipes"
           data-cro="yoga-hygiene-hero-secondary-cta">
          Shop Yoga Studio Wipes
        </a>
      </div>
    </div>
  </header><section class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip" aria-label="What members notice">
    <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__item">
      <h2 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__t">Clean Mats</h2>
      <p>Member-facing cleanliness is the first thing people feel underfoot.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__item">
      <h2 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__t">Clean Props</h2>
      <p>Shared blocks, straps, and bolsters need consistent wipe-downs.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__item">
      <h2 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__t">Visible Standards</h2>
      <p>Members notice how organized and cared-for the studio looks.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__item">
      <h2 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-strip__t">Easy Access</h2>
      <p>Cleaning supplies belong exactly where the cleaning happens.</p>
    </div>
  </section>

    </nav><section id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-expect" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-sec">
      <h2>What Members Expect From Yoga Studio Hygiene</h2>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-split">
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-split__text">
          <p>Members rarely see your cleaning schedule, but they feel its results in seconds. A mat that smells faintly of sweat, a strap that looks used, or a reception counter with visible grime quietly tells a member how much your studio pays attention — and whether they should renew.</p>
          <p>In practice, members judge yoga studio hygiene through a handful of touchpoints: the <strong>yoga mats</strong> they lie on, the <strong>blocks, straps, and bolsters</strong> they share, the <strong>floors</strong> they walk across barefoot, and the <strong>door handles and reception surfaces</strong> they touch on the way in. Visible <strong>wipe stations</strong> matter too — they signal that cleaning is routine, not reactive.</p>
          <p>This is why hygiene now sits inside the member experience rather than beside it. Consistent, visible cleanliness helps reinforce perceived professionalism, supports trust, and contributes to the overall impression that keeps members coming back. It won't guarantee retention on its own, but in a boutique wellness market where members have options, it's one of the easiest standards to control.</p>
          <a class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-inline-cta" href="/collections/fitness" data-cro="yoga-hygiene-expect-cta">Set Your Studio Standard →</a>
        </div>
        <figure class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-split__media"><img class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-img"
                 src="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/IMG_5517.jpg?v=1787273207&width=800"
                 srcset="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/IMG_5517.jpg?v=1787273207&width=500 500w,
                         //wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/IMG_5517.jpg?v=1787273207&width=800 800w,
                         //wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/IMG_5517.jpg?v=1787273207&width=1200 1200w"
                 sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 40vw"
                 width="1206"
                 height="1809"
                 alt="Yoga members setting up on freshly cleaned mats before class"
                 loading="lazy" decoding="async"></figure>
      </div>
    </section><section id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-standards" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-sec">
      <h2>Yoga Studio Hygiene Standards to Follow in 2026</h2>
      <p class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-lead">Members increasingly expect a defined, repeatable standard — not occasional deep cleans. These six studio cleaning standards form a practical baseline for boutique studios and multi-location operators alike.</p>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-grid wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-grid--3">
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-card">
          <h3>Clean Between Classes</h3>
          <p>Wipe mats and shared props during class turnover so the next group starts on a fresh surface.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-card">
          <h3>Keep Shared Props Ready</h3>
          <p>Blocks, straps, and bolsters should be visibly cleaned and organized between sessions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-card">
          <h3>Make Supplies Accessible</h3>
          <p>Place wipes at the studio entrance, prop shelf, and reception so cleaning is frictionless.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-card">
          <h3>Standardize High-Touch Cleaning</h3>
          <p>Define exactly which door handles, counters, and surfaces get wiped and how often.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-card">
          <h3>Keep Backup Inventory</h3>
          <p>Set a minimum stock level so you never run out mid-week or during peak periods.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-card">
          <h3>Train Staff on One Routine</h3>
          <p>Every instructor should follow the same steps, so the standard holds across every shift.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section><section id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-what" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-sec">
      <h2>What Surfaces and Equipment Should a Yoga Studio Clean?</h2>
      <p class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-lead">A useful yoga studio cleaning checklist starts with mapping every shared and high-touch point. Always follow the manufacturer's care guidance for the specific material.</p>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-grid wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-grid--auto"><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Yoga mats</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Blocks</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Straps</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Bolsters</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Blankets & shared textiles</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Studio floors</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Door handles</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Reception surfaces</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Water station & high-touch areas</div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-chip">Shared equipment</div></div>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-callout">
        <strong>High-touch surfaces most frequently missed:</strong> the back of prop shelves, cubby handles, light switches, and the underside of mat edges. These are exactly the spots members notice when a studio looks "almost" clean.
      </div>
    </section><section id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-often" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-sec">
      <h2>How Often Should a Yoga Studio Clean?</h2>
      <p class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-lead">Frequency should scale with traffic, class volume, and how much equipment is shared. Use this as a starting framework, then adjust to your studio and any local requirements.</p>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq">
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__row"><span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__tag">Between Classes</span><p>Wipe shared mats and props; clear the space for the next group.</p></div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__row"><span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__tag">Daily</span><p>Clean floors, door handles, reception, and all high-touch surfaces.</p></div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__row"><span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__tag">Weekly</span><p>Run a deeper clean of textiles and shelving; review inventory levels.</p></div>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__row"><span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-freq__tag">Monthly</span><p>Audit standards, staff compliance, supplies, and replenishment cadence.</p></div>
      </div>
      <p class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-note">Exact frequency depends on traffic, class volume, equipment sharing, manufacturer guidance, and local requirements. Treat the above as an operational baseline, not a universal regulation.</p>
    </section><section id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-stations" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-sec">
      <h2>Why Cleaning Stations Matter</h2>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-split wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-split--rev">
        <figure class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-split__media"><img class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-img"
                 src="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/Design_sem_nome_-_2026-08-18T161139.541.png?v=1787080696&width=800"
                 srcset="//wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/Design_sem_nome_-_2026-08-18T161139.541.png?v=1787080696&width=500 500w,
                         //wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/Design_sem_nome_-_2026-08-18T161139.541.png?v=1787080696&width=800 800w,
                         //wipex.co/cdn/shop/files/Design_sem_nome_-_2026-08-18T161139.541.png?v=1787080696&width=1200 1200w"
                 sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 40vw"
                 width="975"
                 height="1463"
                 alt="Staff member wiping a yoga mat with studio cleaning wipes between classes"
                 loading="lazy" decoding="async"></figure>
        <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-split__text">
          <p>The fastest way to raise your standard isn't asking staff to try harder — it's removing friction. When wipes live at the studio door, prop shelf, and reception, cleaning happens naturally during turnover instead of getting skipped when classes run tight.</p>
          <p>Dedicated cleaning stations also make the standard <em>visible</em>. Members see that wiping down is routine, and staff always know where supplies are. For busy studios, a station model with backup inventory is the difference between a standard that holds and one that quietly slips during peak weeks.</p>
          <a class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-inline-cta" href="/collections/fitness" data-cro="yoga-hygiene-stations-cta">Build Your Cleaning Stations →</a>

    </section><section id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-sec">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq" data-wpxyh-faq><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-1">
                <span>What are the hygiene standards for a yoga studio?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-1" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>Yoga studio hygiene standards in 2026 center on visible, repeatable cleaning: wiping mats and shared props between classes, cleaning floors and high-touch surfaces daily, keeping supplies accessible at cleaning stations, maintaining backup inventory, and training all staff on one routine. The goal is a consistent standard members can see and feel every visit.</p>
            </div>
          </div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-2">
                <span>How often should a yoga studio clean its mats?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-2" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>Shared studio mats should be wiped between classes and cleaned daily, with a deeper weekly clean. Exact frequency depends on class volume, how much the mats are shared, and manufacturer care guidance. Higher-traffic studios should wipe more often to keep every group starting on a fresh surface.</p>
            </div>
          </div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-3">
                <span>What should yoga studios clean between classes?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-3" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>Between classes, wipe down shared yoga mats, blocks, straps, and bolsters, plus high-touch points like door handles and the prop shelf. Clearing and cleaning during turnover keeps the standard visible and ensures the next group starts on clean equipment.</p>
            </div>
          </div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-4">
                <span>What are the best wipes for yoga mats in a studio?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-4" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>The best wipes for a studio are equipment-safe and made for the materials in yoga spaces — gentle on mats, rubber, and foam, without slippery films. At studio volume, prioritize cost per wipe, high count, and a dispensing format that works at a station. Plant-based, low-odor wipes like Wipex fit daily studio use.</p>
            </div>
          </div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-5">
                <span>Are bulk wipes better for busy yoga studios?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-5" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>For busy studios, yes. Bulk wipes lower cost per wipe, reduce reorders, and keep one consistent product across every station. That consistency makes it easier to hold your standard during peak weeks and to plan predictable replenishment instead of reacting to shortages.</p>
            </div>
          </div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-6">
                <span>What cleaning supplies does a yoga studio need?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-6" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>A yoga studio needs equipment-safe wipes for mats and props, supplies for floors and high-touch surfaces, dispensing stations placed where cleaning happens, and backup inventory. Bulk formats and a standard reorder cadence keep every station stocked without last-minute scrambling.</p>
            </div>
          </div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-7">
                <span>How should yoga studios clean shared props?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-7" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>Clean shared props — blocks, straps, and bolsters — with equipment-safe wipes between uses, and give textiles like blankets and bolster covers a deeper clean on a weekly schedule. Always follow the manufacturer care guidance for each material to protect the equipment.</p>
            </div>
          </div><div class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__item">
            <h3 class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__q">
              <button type="button" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__btn" data-wpxyh-faq-btn aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-8">
                <span>How can a yoga studio standardize cleaning across multiple locations?</span>
                <span class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__ic" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
              </button>
            </h3>
            <div id="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq-8" class="wpxyh-template23272641495283blogyogahygieneaiH4URzL-faq__a" data-wpxyh-faq-panel hidden>
              <p>Multi-location operators standardize by choosing one consistent product, purchasing in bulk centrally, setting a predictable replenishment schedule, and documenting one cleaning routine every location follows. This keeps hygiene consistent across sites and makes the standard easy to train and audit as you scale.</p>
            </div>
          </div></div>

  <script>
function getVariantFromURL() {
    const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    const variant = urlParams.get('variant');
    console.log("Extracted Variant ID:", variant);
    return variant;
}

function getProductIdFromLoopWidget() {
    if (typeof LOOP_WIDGET === 'undefined') {
        console.log("LOOP_WIDGET is not defined.");
        return null;
    }

    const productIds = Object.keys(LOOP_WIDGET);
    if (productIds.length === 0) {
        console.log("No product ID found in LOOP_WIDGET.");
        return null;
    }

    const pid = productIds[0];
    console.log("Extracted Product ID from LOOP_WIDGET:", pid);
    return pid;
}

function handleVariantChange() {
    const variantId = getVariantFromURL();
    if (!variantId) {
        console.log("No variant ID found in URL.");
        return;
    }

    const pid = getProductIdFromLoopWidget();
    if (!pid) {
        console.log("Failed to get product ID.");
        return;
    }

    const inputElement = document.querySelector('input[name="product-id"]');
    if (inputElement && window?.LoopSubscriptions) {
        setTimeout(() => {
            console.log(
                "Updating LoopSubscriptions with product ID:",
                inputElement.value,
                "and variant ID:",
                variantId
            );
            window.LoopSubscriptions.handleLoopWidgetVariantIdChange(
                Number(inputElement.value),
                Number(variantId)
            );
        }, 0);
    } else {
        console.warn("LoopSubscriptions or product-id input not available.");
    }
}

// Run on page load
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", handleVariantChange);

// Listen for SPA URL changes (history API manipulation)
(function () {
    let lastUrl = location.href;

    new MutationObserver(() => {
        if (location.href !== lastUrl) {
            lastUrl = location.href;
            console.log("URL changed, re-running variant check.");
            handleVariantChange();
        }
    }).observe(document, { subtree: true, childList: true });

    window.addEventListener('popstate', handleVariantChange);
})();
</script>
